rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uranus and Neptune's discovery did not refute the Quran's statements about seven heavens; science instead uncovered facts that help clarify them.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ın yedi semâ hakkındaki nusûsuna karşı da âlem-i fen ve tecribede mugāyir bir şey isbat olunmamış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because height and depth are relative to the observing point, the numbers of heavens and earths vary in proportion, as 65:12 states.
rows.anchor: Ve hepsinde arz adedi de semâ adediyle mütenâsib bulunur وَمِنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّ [et-Talâk 65/12] düstûru şaşmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With equivalent visibility, an observer at Venus would count eight heavens, at Mercury nine, and at the Sun ten.
rows.anchor: sekiz semâ sekiz arz hesab etmiş olacaktık, bu suretle Utârid’den baksa idik bu aded dokuz olacaktı, Şems’ten baksa idik tam on adedine çıkacaktı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Observers at other bodies would need sharper vision to see the extra layers; otherwise they would still stop at the seven visible from Earth.
rows.anchor: Fakat onlardan bakarak bunları görebilmek için gözlerimizin daha fazla incelikleri seçebilecek derecede kuvvetli olması iktizâ edecekti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking the Sun as center, Earth as sixth, and the tenth heaven as the encompassing boundary yields two paired earth-and-heaven frames, for the solar system and fixed stars.
rows.anchor: biri de sevâbite ait olmak üzere iki arz ve iki semâ saymamız lâzım geleceği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If all celestial bodies are treated as one point within all space, the same relative scheme reduces to one earth and one heaven; the terms express above-and-below relation.
rows.anchor: ancak bir arz ile bir semâ hesab etmiş oluruz ki, ale’l-ıtlâk arz ve semâ denildiği zaman bir taht ve fevk tekabülünden ibaret olan bir ikilik ifade edilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A body is conceived through six directional points arranged around a seventh center, whose intersections yield the three dimensions.
rows.anchor: muhîtte altı ciheti tâyin eden altı nokta olup bunlardan yedincisi olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sevenfold arrangement of relation and unification is indispensable: without bringing the surrounding points into unity in oneself, one cannot conceive any body.
rows.anchor: yedi adedinin tasnîfiyle kendimde bir vahdet bulmadan ne en küçük ne de en büyük

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After reaching the physical horizon, consciousness recognizes its own worth and strives to rise beyond confinement in the material sphere.
rows.anchor: rûh ve şuurumun kıymetini tanımış olduğum cihetle, ben kendimde o cismânî muhîte

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In spiritual contemplation, the heart is the earth-like center within the sky of consciousness, with seven openings to the surrounding world that awaken faith and will.
rows.anchor: kalbimizde iman ve irade şuuru uyandırmak üzere muhît ile alâkadar yedi pencere buluruz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Five openings are the senses, the sixth is reason and logic, and the seventh is the wider faculty of inspiration and revelation.
rows.anchor: yedincisi herkeste sarih ve kavî olmamakla beraber hepsinden geniş olan ilham ve vahiy kuvveleridir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels are hidden benevolent material and spiritual forces that clear obstacles and strengthen perception, faith, and will as spirit flows through the faculties.
rows.anchor: “melâike” denilen birçok gizli ve hayırlı maddî ve mânevî kuvvetler bulunduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn and satans are harmful forces that obstruct spiritual influx and mislead people through distortions of judgment, imagination, ideas, dreams, or impressions.
rows.anchor: birtakım şer ve alçak kuvvetler de vardır ki bunlara da cin ve şeytan denilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Misjudging friend and foe, truth and error, or good and evil, as well as misleading dreams and words, are described as satanic interference between people and heaven.
rows.anchor: hep gizli veya açık bir şeytan parmağıdır ki bunlar bizimle semâ arasında icrâ-yı şekāvet ederler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without these harmful forces, people would make no error in feeling or willing and would conform to truth in every matter.
rows.anchor: Bunlar olmasaydı biz hiçbir his ve irademizde hata etmez, her hususta hakka intibak ederdik.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Protection depends on innate capacity, the strength of spiritual influx in proportion to that capacity, and the degree to which its contents agree up to the source of revelation.
rows.anchor: üçüncüsü de iradenin hudûdunda bu vâridâtın ta menba‘-ı vahye kadar yekdiğerine mutabakatlarının derecesi gözetilmek lâzımdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seven layered perceptual worlds correspond to touch, taste, smell, hearing, sight, reason, and inspiration or revelation, integrating the self with its outer world.
rows.anchor: lâmise muhîti, zâika muhîti, şâmme muhîti, sâmi‘a muhîti, bâsıra muhîti, akl u mantık muhîti, ilham ve vahiy muhîti demek olan bu yedi âlem

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God, though absent from ordinary sensation and observation, is sensed and known through the faith and gnosis that arise when outward and inward realities correspond.
rows.anchor: vücûd-i Hak da böyle bütün zâhir ile bâtının intibâkı noktasından doğan iman ve irfan nûruyla sezilir, tanınır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The physical survey rises from planetary orbits to a relative sixth-heaven boundary at the solar system, then views the countless fixed stars under the seventh heaven as the bodily horizon.
rows.anchor: bütün Manzûme-i Şemsiye hudûdu nihâyetinde altıncı semâda nisbî bir müntehâ bularak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He posits a relative Sidrat al-Muntaha at the sixth heaven, ending the solar system, and an absolute one at the seventh, ending the bodily universe.
rows.anchor: birisi arzımızdan altıncı semâda manzûmemize nihâyet veren nisbî bir sidre-i müntehâ, birisi de yedinci semâda âlem-i cismânîye nihâyet veren umûmî bir sidre-i müntehâ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spiritual contemplation has a sixth-heaven endpoint in the realm of intelligibles and a broader seventh-heaven endpoint in inspiration and revelation.
rows.anchor: birisi yine altıncı semâ olan ma‘kūlât muhîti müntehâsı, birisi de daha geniş olan yedinci semâda ilham ve vahiy muhîti müntehâsı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mi'raj reports in Sahih Muslim place the Sidra in the sixth heaven in one account and the seventh in others; he reconciles them as two Sidrat al-Muntahas.
rows.anchor: sahih olan bu iki hadîsin cem‘inden yedi semâda iki sidre-i müntehâ bulunduğu anlaşılır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mi'raj should be understood in both bodily and spiritual respects, combining both perspectives on the seven heavens.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah’ın mi‘râcı hem cismânî hem rûhânî olmak haysiyetiyle de yedi semâ hakkında bu iki haysiyeti câmi‘bir görüş tâkip etmek lâzım gelir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Physical sight ends at the visible sky, while intellect and revelation extend contemplation beyond bodily heavens to the Kursi and Throne encompassing heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: Kürsî ve Arş muhîtine kadar yükselen bir sidre-i müntehâ ifade etmektedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first command to return the gaze marks the limit of bodily vision; the second, introduced by thumma, marks the spiritual limits that neither sensation nor intellect can encompass.
rows.anchor: rûhânî âleme ait nazar hadlerini basar ve basîrete tanıtmaktadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In both bodily and spiritual surveys, the observer's gaze remains within seven heavens and reaches an endpoint from relative toward absolute.
rows.anchor: Biz bunların her birinde muhtelif merâtib-i vücûdun derece derece yekdiğerine mutabakatları nizâmı içinde bizimle intibakları noktasında bulunarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Correspondence between levels of existence gives awareness of God's unity, the vastness of His dominion, and one's own limits and destination.
rows.anchor: kendimizle âfâkımız arasında duyduğumuz vahdet şuurundan Zât-ı Hakk’ın birliğini ve mülk-i Hakk’ın vüs‘at ve azametini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who use only a bodily perspective anthropomorphize God's istiwa upon the Throne, imagining Him as a body above the created bodily universe.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın Arş üzerinde istivâsını bir cism-i kül hâlinde mülâhaza olunan mahluk âlemin üzerinde hiçbir cisme benzemez diğer bir cisim gibi farzederler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That view makes divine knowledge seem wider and greater than God's essence; God's exaltation is essential and real, not spatial or bodily.
rows.anchor: bu yükseklik mekânî ve cismânî değil, zâtî ve hakīkīdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who consider only the spiritual realm picture God as a universal spirit but fail to recognize that He is greater than both the bodily and spiritual totalities.
rows.anchor: Zât-ı Hakk’ın her ikisinden daha yüksek ve daha büyük وَهُوَ ٱلْعَلِىُّ ٱلْكَبِيرُ [Sebe’ 34/23] olması lâzım geleceğini düşünmezler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abstract thinkers can fall into a low unity by erasing God within themselves instead of losing themselves in God and rising to transcendent unity.
rows.anchor: kendilerini Hak’ta ifnâ ederek müte‘âlî bir vahdete yükselecek yerde Hakk’ı kendilerinde ifnâ etmek suretiyle sâfil bir vahdete düşerler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not perceived unless mind and reality, inner and outer, and the spiritual and bodily realms meet in correspondence at one point.
rows.anchor: zihin ile vâki‘, enfüs ile âfak, rûhânî âlem ile cismânî âlem bir noktada intibak etmeyince Hak sezilmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spirit and body are not God but signs pointing to God's existence; God alone has power and witness over all, and every matter returns to Him.
rows.anchor: rûh ve cisim ayn-ı Hak değil, mülk-i ilâhîde vücûd-i Hakk’a dâl birer âyettirler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To gain a glimpse of God's majesty in His essence and oneness, one must be overcome at the boundary where bodily and spiritual realms correspond and vanish in God's unity.
rows.anchor: âlem-i cismânî ile âlem-i rûhânînin birbirine muntabık olarak vahdet-i Hak’ta fâni oldukları bir sidre-i müntehâda gaşyolmak lâzımdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Body and spirit are two wings toward nearness to God; the manifestation of the Merciful beyond their joined endpoint encompasses the whole Throne of existence.
rows.anchor: müstevâ-yı Rahmân bu iki kanadın yumulduğu sidre-i müntehânın fevkinden tecellî ederek bütün Arş-ı vücûdu ihâta ve istîlâ eyler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The delayed thumma opens room for spiritual reflection, and karratayn signals that the command joins the two perspectives of bodily and spiritual contemplation.
rows.anchor: iki nokta-i nazarın cem‘ine işaret olunarak da bilhassa كَرَّتَيْنِ kaydı ile takyid edilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the endpoint, divine manifestations overwhelm the observer in fana fillah; awakening with baqa billah, the observer returns to the self as the starting point of full servitude.
rows.anchor: tecelliyât-ı ilâhiyenin azameti karşısında kendinden geçip fenâ fillah ile istiğrak hâlinde bîtâb olarak uyandıktan sonra neticede bekā billah şuuru ile
